text.p: Computer software firm Baan Company NV is positive about the outlook for 1997 following a surge in 1996 profits and sees markets continuing to grow over the year, its founder and chief executive said on Wednesday.

"The market is there and the market is growing reasonably -- (at) 40 percent -- we're able to grow faster than the market," Jan Baan told journalists after a presentation to discuss the firm's 1996 results which were announced a week ago.
"You've seen from the figures we're able to grow fast, increasing all our performance indicators, we believe that we are well positioned for growth," he said.

Baan makes software for businesses that allow users to gather and integrate information and then apply it in their own business practices. It has more than 2,000 customers worldwide including The Boeing Company and Hitachi Ltd.
In 1996 net profit ballooned to $36.34 million from $15.28 million, with licence revenue, and maintenance and service revenue nearly doubling to $224.24 million and $152.43 million.

Fourth quarter net profit of $15.85 million outstripped 1995's profit for the full year, as markets boomed and service and maintenance margins climbed to 21 percent in the fourth quarter from 15 percent in the first quarter.
Overall operating income margins rose to 15 percent from 11 percent in 1996, finance director Jan Westerhoud told reporters.
Baan was asked about new contracts and whether he believed the company could sustain the growth seen over 1996, when total revenues surged to $388 million from $216 million.
"Managing growth will not be a problem. Like always the pipeline is good and continues improving," he replied.

Baan shares by midsession on Wednesday were 1.30 guilders higher at 85.00 guilders, up from 80.00 guilders a week ago. The shares have surged on the Amsterdam bourse since the beginning of the year, starting 1997 at 61.00 guilders.
